items.html:
One of the most common things we hear from curly-haired clients before they've ever sat in our chair is some version of: "I didn't think extensions were really for me." Usually that's because somewhere along the line, they either saw a bad blend, or they were told their texture was "too difficult" to work with. Neither of those things is true when it's done by someone who actually understands curl patterns — and hair extensions for curly hair are one of the areas we get the most consistently thrilled reactions from clients.

The Real Challenge Isn't the Curl — It's the Match

The single biggest thing that makes or breaks curly extensions isn't the method, it's whether the extension hair's curl pattern actually matches yours. Human hair extensions can be steamed and set into a curl pattern, but that pattern needs to be assessed and matched to your natural texture before installation — not just picked off a shelf. This is why we spend real time in a curly-hair consultation looking closely at your curl diameter, density, and how tight or loose your pattern is at the root versus the ends.

Methods That Actually Work With Curls

Not every extension method handles texture equally well. For curly and textured hair, we typically recommend:

●        Natural Beaded Rows (hand-tied wefts): installed to sit low and blend into the curl pattern, ideal for adding volume without flattening your natural shape.

●        K-Tip Extensions: individually bonded strands move independently, which mimics how curls naturally clump and separate far better than a flat weft can.

●        Microlink Extensions: work well for finer curl patterns and allow precise placement around the crown and part.

●        Brazilian Knots Extensions: exceptionally durable and specifically well-suited to curly and natural hair textures that need a strong, long-lasting hold.

What About Shrinkage and Styling?

This is the part a lot of salons get wrong. Curly hair "shrinks" — the length you see at full curl definition is shorter than the strand's true length — and extensions need to be selected and cut with that in mind, or you'll end up with mismatched length once everything springs up. We factor curl shrinkage into every measurement and cut, so the length you're promised is the length you actually see once your curls settle into their natural pattern.

Caring for Curly Extensions Day to Day

Curl-friendly extension care isn't dramatically different from caring for your natural curls — moisture is still your best friend. We'll walk you through a wash and styling routine specific to your combined natural-and-extension hair, including how to detangle without disrupting the blend and which products actually work with (not against) both textures.

You Don't Have to Choose Between Length and Your Curls

The idea that you have to straighten your hair to wear extensions successfully is outdated, and frankly, it's not something we ever want a client to feel pressured into. With the right match, method, and cut, your curls stay exactly your curls — just longer, fuller, and every bit as bouncy as before.

Come in for a unhurried consultation and we'll show you exactly what your curl pattern paired with the right extension method could look like. Book online or call (212) 221-3881.
